g.text: Two breadboards and the Breadboard Helper go here. No holes.

Keypad LCD Helper H3, to the Cable Bridge
Keypad Helper H1, to the Cable Bridge
Plate hole used by this build: a screw through the board into a standoff.
Plate hole for a printed part.
Plate hole this build doesn't use.
On the Cable Bridge: the board has a hole here and the plate doesn't. The board screws to the
Resting: the board has a hole here and the plate doesn't. The standoff stands on the plate.
Added for the KIM Board. On an older plate, drill this hole by hand through all three layers: Ø3.2
The Hanger is optional on both builds, for hanging the computer on a wall. The Hanger goes on the back of
the plate and the Hanger Retainer on top.
The Cable Bridge is only for the four-board build. Standoffs at S1 and S2 would block the 40-pin BUS ribbon
cable, which runs under the boards from the Backplane Helper to the Breadboard Helper, so those two board
holes screw to the bridge instead. The bridge goes on top of the plate and the Cable Bridge Retainer on the
back. The KIM Board needs neither the bridge nor the cable: S2 is a standoff to the plate.
The plate is a stack of three 3 mm acrylic layers, each cut from Plate.svg. Plate.svg is drawn turned 180°
The SVG is drawn 1:1, so it can be printed at full size to check a plate.
M2.5 × 10 standoff, female-female, for the LCD
M2.5 × 6 pan head, for the LCD
A normal hole, from the bottom up: an M3 × 12 pan head through the back of the plate, a female-male
standoff, the board, a female-female standoff, the top, and an M3 × 6 pan head.
Hole 19 on the KIM Board has no top above it: a female-female standoff instead, with an M3 × 6 pan head
The KIM Board's counts are for its new top, over holes 3, 5, 7, 8, 13, 14, 16, 20, 21 and S2.
S2 on the KIM Board: a female-male standoff stands on the plate with no screw below it.
S1 and S2 on the four-board build: an M3 × 8 countersunk screw comes up through the Cable Bridge and the
board into a female-female standoff, then the top.
Corners, the Cable Bridge and the Hanger: an M3 × 16 countersunk screw from the top, through the plate,
into a nut in the part below.
The LCD: a standard socket and pin header, on female-female M2.5 × 10 standoffs with an M2.5 washer on
each to make up the height. An M2.5 × 6 pan head goes in each end of each standoff, above the LCD and
Rubber feet: one in the Ø10 recess under each Corner.
One plate takes either build. Looking down on the plate, as the computer is used. All dimensions in mm.
